actions.action: Send a clearer close-up of the leaves and flowers or say where the plant was bought, to confirm the ID
Move the plant to a brighter spot or give it a few hours of direct sun
Check whether the soil stays wet for long stretches
Pull out the Kalanchoe stowaways, including plantlets in the soil, and keep them away from pets
If repotting, repot in spring or early summer into cactus mix with perlite, one pot size up
Gently tease out the roots and check for rot
If roots are brown and mushy, trim them off
Wait a few days after repotting, then water

reason: The answer mentions competition and nutrient issues only as secondary possibilities, with light as the main cause; its repotting advice calls for an even faster-draining cactus mix and says repotting may be unnecessary, the opposite of the less-draining soil that fixed the plant, so the advice is harmful.
